description: We are building HydroWatch Global (AquaSentinel), a satellite platform monitoring drought and water contraction in hydroelectric infrastructure. Using NASA data (Landsat, GPM, SMAP, SWOT, MODIS) for risk indexing, we provide early warnings for grids like the Zambezi Basin. Join us to build an interactive mapping tool. We seek teammates skilled in web development, Python/Google Earth Engine geospatial analysis, machine learning, or hydrology.
summary: HydroWatch Global (AquaSentinel) is a web application that acts as a trend detective for the water that feeds hydropower dams. Using 45 years of NASA POWER data (1981–2025), it tests whether rainfall, soil moisture, temperature and related variables are really changing over a catchment, shows where the change is happening on a map, and reports whether the trend is statistically significant.The tool answers the four core questions of the “Be An Earth System Trend Detective!” challenge: what is changing, where it is changing, how much it is changing, and whether the change is significant. It combines least-squares trend analysis with an autocorrelation-corrected t-test, Mann-Kendall with Sen’s slope, false-discovery-rate control on the map, and a Pettitt step-change test. On top sits a Hydro Stress Index that acts as an early-warning signal for drought risk to reservoir inflows.The app runs fully offline after the first data fetch, needs no account or API key, and was verified with 545 statistical checks against SciPy. It was built first for the Kariba catchment in Zambia, where slow drying upstream has already translated into severe power cuts.
details:
HydroWatch Global is an installable web application that lets users select a hydropower catchment (or any custom region), choose one of 12 NASA variables, and instantly see:

  • A plain-language verdict (Significant / Borderline / Not significant)
  • A time-series chart with trend line, Sen’s slope and 95% confidence band
  • A map showing which 50 km grid cells are drying or wetting
  • A Hydro Stress Index that flags drought risk to reservoir inflows
  • One-click export of PNG charts, CSV data and a one-page PDF report

How it works
A small local Python server fetches and caches NASA POWER monthly data. All statistics run in the browser using a statistics engine written from scratch (no external statistics library). The same code is tested against SciPy reference values (545 checks passed).

Tools & stack

  • Backend: Python 3 standard library only
  • Frontend: Vanilla JavaScript (ES modules), Leaflet, Chart.js
  • Statistics: Custom implementation of t-test (with autocorrelation correction), Mann-Kendall, Sen’s slope, Seasonal Kendall, Pettitt test, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR
  • Optional overlays: GPM IMERG rainfall and SMAP soil moisture (require free Earthdata login)

Benefits & impact
The tool turns complex, long-term NASA climate data into a clear, honest answer that students, journalists, planners and researchers can understand. It was designed first around the Kariba catchment — a high-stakes real-world case where upstream drying has already caused severe electricity shortages in Zambia and Zimbabwe.

Creativity

  • Statistics engine written from scratch and fully verified
  • Offline-first Progressive Web App
  • Dual independent significance tests + explicit “Borderline” category for honesty
  • Catchment-focused early-warning index on top of pure trend detection
